companyDescription: Quantum-safe semiconductors · WISeKey-affiliated post-quantum secure chip platform (QS7001, QVault TPM) building the Quantum Spatial Orbital Cloud (QSOC) — a satellite-based post-quantum security network whose first dedicated satellite is planned on a SpaceX mission in Q4 2026 · ~$463M cash vs ~$340M market cap
priceNote: Live $1.46 (+2.6%) on Nov 11, 2026 — down 36% from $2.28 at the Sep 29 report, near the bottom of a ~$1.42–$7.26 52-week range. Market cap ~$340M (~231M shares) sits BELOW the ~$463M of cash reported at Sep 30. Old Base +35% ($3.08) is replaced by a new Base +40% ($2.04) anchored to the live price.
summary: Refresh after a -36% slide since the Sep 29 report: nothing in the thesis broke — the Oct 15 nine-month update reaffirmed FY2026 revenue guidance of $27–36M (9M revenue $16.3M, implying a record $11–20M Q4) and reported ~$463M of cash at Sep 30 — but the stock now trades at ~$340M, below its own cash pile, dragged by the quantum-sector de-rate (B. Riley cut RGTI and QBTS targets Nov 2) and a hawkish rate tape. The first dedicated QSOC satellite is still guided for a SpaceX mission in Q4 2026 with no confirmed launch date (a November date appears only in secondary coverage). That makes this a cash-backed option on two near-term proofs: the satellite reaching orbit and Q4 revenue landing inside guidance. Measured turbo median return to just after the catalyst is -10.6% (n=69), so the preferred entry is the dip zone, not today's price. Size 2–4% of portfolio max.

catalysts.name: QSOC First Satellite Launch (SpaceX)
catalysts.description: First dedicated Quantum Spatial Orbital Cloud satellite on a SpaceX mission — the initial node of a post-quantum security / digital-identity network the company plans to scale to as many as 100 satellites by 2033. Company guidance is Q4 2026; no exact launch date confirmed.

catalysts.name: FY2026 Revenue vs $27–36M Guidance
catalysts.description: The Oct 15 nine-month update put 9M revenue at $16.3M and reaffirmed $27–36M for FY2026, implying $11–20M in Q4 (vs $8.4M in Q4 2025). Initial QS7001 / QVault TPM commercial revenue is expected toward the end of H2 2026.

catalysts.name: Nine-Month 2026 Revenue Update
catalysts.description: Preliminary 9M 2026 revenue $16.3M (+65% YoY), cash ~$463M at Sep 30, FY2026 guidance reaffirmed.

risks: QSOC launch is only guided to 'Q4 2026' on a SpaceX mission with no confirmed date — a slip into 2027 is a real possibility for a first-of-its-kind deployment, and the thesis loses its near-term proof point if it slips.
Implied Q4 revenue of $11–20M is a wide range and depends on QS7001 / QVault TPM commercial revenue starting late in H2 2026; landing at the low end would undercut the growth narrative.

Cash fell from ~$486M (Jun 30) to ~$463M (Sep 30), and part of the balance sheet is committed to strategic investments and the $200M Quantum Fund (EeroQ, Quobly and others) rather than SEALSQ's own execution — cash-above-market-cap overstates what is freely deployable.
Share count grew ~16.7% from Dec 2025 to mid-2026 on capital raises; further dilution to fund satellites and the Quantum Fund is a structural feature of the model.
High beta to quantum-sector sentiment (RGTI, IONQ, QBTS): the -36% since Sep 29 happened without company-specific bad news, and could continue the same way.

estimateDates.note: Company guidance Q4 2026; no confirmed launch date

macroRisk.rateOutlook: The Fed hiked 25bp on Sep 16, 2026 (first hike since 2023), and a hot October CPI (core +0.3% m/m vs 0.2% expected) has pushed Dec 9 FOMC hike odds to roughly 89–100%, with the 10-year near 4.98%.
macroRisk.inflationNote: October CPI ran hot (headline +0.4% m/m, core +0.3%); October PCE on Nov 25 is the next inflation read.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: Higher-for-longer compresses multiples on long-duration quantum/post-quantum names, and LAES trades with RGTI/IONQ/QBTS sentiment. The offset is unusual: ~$463M of cash against a ~$340M market cap means no financing pressure from tighter conditions.
macroRisk.summary: MEDIUM — a priced-in December hike and a ~5% 10-year weigh on speculative tech, and sector beta can drag LAES regardless of news, but a balance sheet larger than the market cap removes the financing-driven downside that would push this to HIGH.

entryStrategy.verdict: SPECULATIVE — cash (~$463M) exceeds the market cap (~$340M), with a Q4 2026 QSOC launch and a guided record Q4 as near-term proof points. Measured turbo median return from report price to just after the catalyst is -10.6% (n=69), so buying at report price is not the default: prefer the $1.30–1.40 dip zone. Moonshot sizing 2–4%.

catalystSpot.preRunup: product_launch in the turbo lane has n=7 complete windows (median excess vs SPY +10.5pp, above the +7.7 overall — not a laggard). Hardware first-launch names in space/semis tend to build in the final weeks once a launch window is confirmed; LAES has no confirmed date yet, so any run-up likely starts only after SpaceX manifest confirmation.
catalystSpot.preRunupTiming: 2–4 weeks before a confirmed launch date (sector pattern, not LAES-specific)

postWin.note: No LAES first-launch precedent yet; same-sector quantum validation events are the reference: RGTI rallied up to ~545% over the trailing year to Dec 2025 on federal quantum-investment validation, and IONQ gained 50%+ from end-March 2026 on federal investment news plus the NVIDIA quantum research center partnership.

postLose.note: No LAES launch-failure precedent; uses product_launch's measured turbo medianMAE of -23.9% (n=7) from skill-feedback generated 2026-11-11.

spotSizing.reason: Cash above market cap supports the upper half of the 2–5% turbo band, but no confirmed launch date and sector beta keep it at 3% rather than 4%.

stopPreCatalyst.note: Roughly at product_launch medianMAE (-23.9%) — accepted because cash per share (~$2.00) sits far above this level

stopPostCatalyst.note: Exit if the launch fails or slips into H2 2027, or if FY2026 revenue lands below the $27M guidance floor

comparableCases.event: Federal quantum-investment validation driving trailing-year re-rate
comparableCases.note: Shows the magnitude a small-cap quantum name can re-rate on tangible government/commercial validation over a sustained period — relevant precedent for what a successful first QSOC satellite launch plus the 'Quantum Made in USA' narrative could do for LAES, though the driver (broad quantum-sector momentum, not one launch event) differs from a single binary catalyst.

comparableCases.event: Federal investment announcements + NVIDIA Accelerated Quantum Research Center partnership
comparableCases.note: Shows the pattern of quantum-sector names rallying on concrete validation/partnership news rather than pure speculation — the same kind of proof-point dynamic a successful, orbit-confirmed QSOC launch would represent for SEALSQ specifically.
